items.title: Zelenskyy accuses SpaceX of lying about Starshield – and says US floated Donbas-for-Nato deal - The Guardian
items.snippet: Zelenskyy accuses SpaceX of lying about Starshield – and says US floated Donbas-for-Nato deal The Guardian
items.summary: A Guardian report by Luke Harding in Kyiv, published 14 November 2026 and last updated at 15:35 CET, says President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused SpaceX of not telling the truth about speed limits on Ukraine’s Starshield service, arguing the curbs appear “political” rather than “technical,” after connections have dropped above 161 km/h (100 mph) across the entire frontline for five days, hindering interception of jet-powered Russian Shahed drones and mid-range strikes, even though SpaceX told Ukraine’s defence ministry it was not imposing any restrictions and called the problem technical. In the same piece, Zelenskyy said U.S. negotiators Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff had asked whether Ukraine would give up the Donbas in exchange for NATO membership or NATO-like security guarantees — a proposal he described as vague and that did not appear to involve U.S. peacekeeping troops on the ground — and he categorically ruled out giving away further land.

items.title: Prediction: 2 Stocks That Will Be Worth More Than SpaceX 5 Years From Now - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: Prediction: 2 Stocks That Will Be Worth More Than SpaceX 5 Years From Now Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A Motley Fool column by Geoffrey Seiler, published 14 November 2026 and syndicated on Yahoo Finance, predicts that Meta Platforms and Broadcom — then valued at about $1.64 trillion and $1.66 trillion — could overtake SpaceX’s roughly $1.9 trillion market cap within five years. He argues SpaceX’s terrestrial data-center build-out and compute rental rates face political and pricing risk, while Meta’s AI-driven ads and Muse agents and Broadcom’s custom AI-chip work (with AI chip revenue seen rising from about $57.5 billion in fiscal 2026 to $230 billion in fiscal 2028) give those two a path to a larger valuation.

items.title: SpaceX's Starship enters Earth's orbit, but booster catch aborted - AFP.com
items.snippet: SpaceX's Starship enters Earth's orbit, but booster catch aborted AFP.com
items.summary: An AFP report, published and later updated on 14 November 2026, says SpaceX’s 15th Starship test flight lifted off from Starbase on Friday afternoon but the Super Heavy booster aborted its planned catch at Launch Pad 2 after detecting a guidance, navigation and control issue, then diverted to the Gulf of Mexico and automatically self-destructed before hitting the water. The article says Starship reached orbit, deployed 26 Starlink satellites, was reported healthy with its heat shield about seven hours after liftoff, and was due back Saturday after more than 22 hours for a first attempt to catch the ship at the tower around 3:20 p.m. (21:20 GMT).

items.title: SpaceX’s Latest Starship Mission Hits Early Setback - WSJ
items.snippet: SpaceX’s Latest Starship Mission Hits Early Setback WSJ
items.summary: The full Wall Street Journal article “SpaceX’s Latest Starship Mission Hits Early Setback” (14 November 2026) could not be fetched because of the paywall, so this summary is from the headline only. It reports an early setback on SpaceX’s latest Starship mission.

items.title: SpaceX’s Starship Just Did Something for Only the 2nd Time. Saturday Could Be Even Bigger. - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: SpaceX’s Starship Just Did Something for Only the 2nd Time. Saturday Could Be Even Bigger. Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A Motley Fool article by Johnny Rice, dated 13 November 2026 and listed in Google News under Yahoo Finance, says Starship Flight 15 lifted off from Starbase at 5:47 p.m. ET, reached orbit at 6:13 p.m. ET — only the second time Starship has done so — and began deploying 26 Starlink satellites, while the Super Heavy booster was diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown and burst into flames. Rice notes SpaceX has not shared details of the booster issue, that a catch of the upper stage is scheduled for 4:17 p.m. ET on Saturday only if systems stay healthy, and that the Space segment was just $1.8 billion of SpaceX’s $14.6 billion in third-quarter revenue.

items.title: SpaceX's Starship soars into orbit after booster malfunction thwarts double catch attempt - PBS
items.snippet: SpaceX's Starship soars into orbit after booster malfunction thwarts double catch attempt PBS
items.summary: A PBS NewsHour piece by Marcia Dunn of the Associated Press, published 13 November 2026, says SpaceX’s attempt to recover the entire Starship stack at the pad was thwarted when Super Heavy v3 Booster 22 malfunctioned, automatically aborted, and ended up exploding after being diverted to the Gulf of Mexico, while the Starship 42 spacecraft still reached orbit. It says this was the first catch attempt for the upgraded 236-foot booster and that, barring further trouble, the ship will try a first-ever return-from-orbit catch Saturday after about 22 hours and 15 laps at roughly 170 miles (275 kilometers), having prepared to deploy 26 of SpaceX’s most advanced Starlink satellites.

items.snippet: SpaceX’s Starship Just Did Something for Only the 2nd Time. Saturday Could Be Even Bigger. The Motley Fool

Rice notes SpaceX has not shared details of the booster issue, that a catch of the upper stage is scheduled for 4:17 p.m. ET on Saturday only if systems stay healthy, and that the Space segment was just $1.8 billion of SpaceX’s $14.6 billion in third-quarter revenue.

items.title: Democratic US senators order Musk to preserve records on Ukraine Starlink access - Reuters
items.snippet: Democratic US senators order Musk to preserve records on Ukraine Starlink access Reuters
items.summary: A Reuters report by Jasper Ward and Carlos Méndez, dated 13 November 2026, says Democratic Sens. Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire and Chris Coons of Delaware told Elon Musk to preserve all records related to SpaceX restrictions on Ukraine’s use of Starlink and Starshield, seeking SpaceX records since 1 September — including communications with the White House and Pentagon — and written confirmation by 30 November that preservation measures are in place. The senators said October and November restrictions raise questions about SpaceX’s control over communications the U.S. government relies on; Reuters notes it previously reported a mid-October limit came from inside the White House, which Secretary of State Marco Rubio disputed, and that President Zelenskiy said on 12 November Ukrainian units had again recorded Starshield disruptions.

No Booster Catch Might Hurt the Stock,” says Friday’s 15th flight of Starship, “the largest rocket ever built by humans,” did not go exactly as planned. The rest of the Barron’s page could not be fetched beyond that opening paragraph, so the article’s specific stock commentary is not summarised here.

items.title: SpaceX launches 15th Starship flight; aborts booster recovery maneuver - NBC News
items.snippet: SpaceX launches 15th Starship flight; aborts booster recovery maneuver NBC News
items.summary: An NBC News report by Reuters and Evan Bush, published and updated 13 November 2026, says SpaceX launched the 15th uncrewed Starship flight from Starbase on Friday but aborted the planned “chopstick” catch of the Super Heavy booster shortly after launch, diverting it to the Gulf of Mexico, where it hovered briefly and exploded a short distance over the sea. SpaceX said the upper stage reached orbit about 27 minutes after launch and began releasing 26 Starlink satellites about 36 minutes in; it was not immediately clear why the booster catch failed, and controllers still hoped to bring the ship back after nearly a day in orbit.

items.title: SpaceX launches milestone Starship flight to demonstrate full reusability of orbit-class rocket - CBS News
items.snippet: SpaceX launches milestone Starship flight to demonstrate full reusability of orbit-class rocket CBS News
items.summary: A CBS News report by William Harwood, updated at 9:10 p.m. ET on 13 November 2026, says SpaceX launched Starship’s 15th test flight from Starbase at 5:47 p.m. ET on a 22-hour mission meant to catch both stages, but a little more than six minutes after liftoff flight controllers diverted the Super Heavy booster to a Gulf Coast splashdown because of a technical problem, and it exploded in a fireball moments before hitting the water. After an 18-minute coast and a short orbital-insertion burn, the upper stage was expected to deploy 26 Version 3 Starlink satellites, and SpaceX still planned a first attempt to catch the ship at the pad, with a de-orbit burn listed at 3:21 p.m. ET on Saturday if systems stayed healthy.

items.title: SpaceX launches Starship in key test flight of massive rocket - CNBC
items.snippet: SpaceX launches Starship in key test flight of massive rocket CNBC
items.summary: A CNBC report by Lora Kolodny, published 13 November 2026, says Starship Flight 15 lifted off from Starbase at 4:47 p.m. local time (5:47 p.m. ET) after FAA launch authorization, but SpaceX aborted the plan to catch and reuse the booster and diverted it to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown, where it burst into flames. The upper stage continued to orbit for a planned 14 trips around Earth and a Saturday landing back at Starbase; Kolodny notes the flight also deployed another 26 Starlink V3 satellites, that William Blair analysts said even a failed catch and a delay of a few months would not be that consequential, and that SpaceX faces fresh criticism over Starshield restrictions in Ukraine.

items.title: SpaceX Could Announce a Deal for Tesla as Soon as December. Here's What It Would Do to SpaceX Stock. - The Motley Fool
items.snippet: SpaceX Could Announce a Deal for Tesla as Soon as December. Here's What It Would Do to SpaceX Stock. The Motley Fool
items.summary: A Motley Fool column by Daniel Sparks, published 13 November 2026 at 4:12 p.m. EST, walks through Bloomberg’s report that SpaceX–Tesla merger talks have moved on to price and control, with an announcement possible as soon as December or in early 2027, and neither company commenting. Using mid-November prices, it estimates SpaceX would need about 11.2 billion new shares to buy Tesla at market value with no premium — growing the share count by around 83% and leaving current SpaceX holders with about 55% of a combined company whose sales would be about two-thirds Tesla, with a much lower operating margin (about 8% versus about 19% for SpaceX alone).

items.title: SpaceX faces key launch test tonight with 'double catch' of Starship and Super Heavy Booster - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: SpaceX faces key launch test tonight with 'double catch' of Starship and Super Heavy Booster Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A Yahoo Finance article by Pras Subramanian, published 13 November 2026, says SpaceX’s Starship Flight 15 is scheduled for Friday night at 5:45 p.m. ET and will attempt a first-time “double catch” of both the Super Heavy booster and the Starship upper stage at Boca Chica, which the company said would be the first full recovery of an orbital launch system, while also deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites that SpaceX says add 1 terabit of capacity each — about equal to ten Falcon 9 V2 Mini launches. Morgan Stanley’s Adam Jonas called the flight “one of the most significant catalysts in SpaceX’s 20+ year history”; the piece notes the stock was up 2% for the week after trading between $148.44 and $135.40, and cites Bloomberg reporting that a SpaceX–Tesla merger could be announced as early as December or slip into early 2027.

items.title: Restoring Boca Chica Beach
items.summary: SpaceX’s 13 November Updates post, titled “Restoring Boca Chica Beach,” says the company has discussed buying about 1,200 acres of Texas Parks and Wildlife land surrounding the Starbase launch facility, with more than half to be permanently protected under a conservation easement, and states clearly that Boca Chica Beach is not part of the proposal and will remain public. It argues the land is largely mudflats and fragile dunes with limited recreation, that securing the perimeter would improve public safety around the launch site, and that sale proceeds would let Texas invest in new parkland in the Rio Grande Valley, while SpaceX commits to permanently conserve about 600 acres and continues beach cleanups and sea-turtle work.
items.timeSource: Official SpaceX post linking the 13 November Updates item

items.title: Double-catch drama: Why Starship's Flight 15 is so important to SpaceX - Space
items.snippet: Double-catch drama: Why Starship's Flight 15 is so important to SpaceX Space
items.summary: A Space.com article by Andrew Jones, published 13 November 2026, says SpaceX is targeting today for Starship Flight 15 — the first attempt to catch the Ship upper stage as well as the Super Heavy booster, which the company calls the “Holy Grail of rocketry” — with a 75-minute window opening at 5:45 p.m. EST, a first catch of a next-gen Super Heavy V3 about 6.5 minutes after liftoff, and, if conditions are met, a Ship catch back at Starbase about 21 hours later after deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites. Jones writes that a successful double catch would be the first full recovery of an orbital launch system, a step toward the roughly 10,000 Starship launches a year SpaceX is targeting by 2030, and quotes Elon Musk saying that if both catches succeed it will mark the first time all parts of an orbital rocket return to Earth intact — “the critical breakthrough needed to make life multiplanetary.”

items.title: SpaceX launches 15th Starship flight with hopes of achieving first round trip - Reuters
items.snippet: SpaceX launches 15th Starship flight with hopes of achieving first round trip Reuters
items.summary: A Reuters report by Joey Roulette, published 13 November 2026, says SpaceX’s 15th Starship flight was scheduled to lift off at 4:45 p.m. CT from Starbase and will try for the first time to catch the upper stage at the Texas launch site rather than ditching it in the ocean, after also returning the Super Heavy booster — a mission that would also be the rocket’s second to deploy operational Starlink satellites. SpaceX secured its FAA launch license hours before the planned liftoff; if the plan holds, the booster would be caught and then moved off the pad so the ship can return after about 22 hours and 14 orbits, with the debut ship catch around 2:45 p.m. CT on Saturday.

items.title: SpaceX's giant rocket may leave NASA in the dust - NPR
items.snippet: SpaceX's giant rocket may leave NASA in the dust NPR
items.summary: An NPR report by Geoff Brumfiel, published 13 November 2026, says SpaceX plans its most ambitious Starship test later today — lift off from South Texas, orbit Earth, and land vertically at the same pad 22 and a half hours later — and that experts warn the shift toward Starship could strand NASA, because SpaceX has said it will stop flying Falcon 9, which launches Dragon, currently the only American spacecraft that can ferry NASA astronauts to and from the ISS. NASA has contracted three additional ISS flights that would only take Dragon through 2028 if flown every six months with no further orders; SpaceX did not comment, its latest report showed about $2.1 billion of launch revenue through September versus $12.8 billion from Starlink and $10.9 billion from AI, and Gwynne Shotwell suggested Boeing’s problem-plagued Starliner (next crewed flight sometime in 2028) could take some of that NASA business.

items.title: NROL-136 Mission - SpaceX
items.snippet: NROL-136 Mission SpaceX
items.summary: SpaceX’s official NROL-136 mission page says the company is targeting Saturday, 21 November 2026 for a Falcon 9 launch of the NROL-136 mission from Space Launch Complex 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base, with a 30-minute window opening at 4:30 a.m. PT and a backup at 4:16 a.m. PT on Sunday, 22 November. It says this will be the 14th flight for the first-stage booster, which previously launched Sentinel-6B, Twilight, NROL-172, Transporter-17, USSF-259 and eight Starlink missions, and that after stage separation the booster is due to land at Landing Zone 4 at Vandenberg.

items.title: SpaceX plans over $74 billion investment in Texas, Arizona AI campuses - Reuters
items.snippet: SpaceX plans over $74 billion investment in Texas, Arizona AI campuses Reuters
items.summary: A Reuters report dated 12 November 2026 says SpaceX plans to invest more than $74 billion in two supercomputing campuses — more than $24 billion at Starbase in Texas and roughly $50 billion in Cochise County, Arizona — expanding an AI business that already generated more than half of third-quarter revenue. The Arizona campus still needs county approval and faces a 2,400-signature petition ahead of a December public hearing, while a Starbase city notice describes a gas-fired power plant and supercomputing facility on about 444 acres, with the City Commission due to consider a property tax abatement on 9 December.

items.title: Elon Musk gives SpaceX stock investors something new to consider - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: Elon Musk gives SpaceX stock investors something new to consider Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A TheStreet article by Hillary Remy and Dana Sullivan Kilroy, dated 12 November 2026 and listed in Google News under Yahoo Finance, says Elon Musk wrote on 8 November that if compute becomes plentiful and cheap, SpaceX revenue will drop, while two days later Deutsche Bank analyst Edison Yu raised his 2028 SpaceX forecasts — EBITDA by $18 billion to $237.1 billion and revenue to $315.3 billion — and kept a Buy rating with a $250 price target on the view that data-center opposition will keep computing power scarce. The piece notes Super Intelligence already accounted for about 52% of SpaceX’s $14.6 billion third-quarter sales, that Musk was answering Chamath Palihapitiya’s claim SpaceX could cancel its Anthropic contract on 90 days’ notice and reprice it, and that CFO Bret Johnsen said compute pricing was slightly above the top of a $30 to $50 per-watt range.

items.title: SpaceX Plans $74 Billion Investment to Build Data Centers in Texas and Arizona - The New York Times
items.snippet: SpaceX Plans $74 Billion Investment to Build Data Centers in Texas and Arizona The New York Times
items.summary: A New York Times report dated 12 November 2026 says SpaceX plans a $74 billion investment to build data centers in Texas and Arizona. That tracks SpaceX’s own 12 November update, which puts more than $24 billion into a self-powered supercompute site at Starbase in the Rio Grande Valley and about $50 billion into a Cochise County, Arizona campus; the NYT page itself did not return a readable full text here, so this summary is from the headline plus that official company update.

items.title: SpaceX’s next move is chasing the unprecedented ‘holy grail’ of rocketry. Here’s what’s at stake - CNN
items.snippet: SpaceX’s next move is chasing the unprecedented ‘holy grail’ of rocketry. Here’s what’s at stake CNN
items.summary: A CNN report by Jackie Wattles, dated 12 November 2026, says SpaceX will try on Friday, in a window from 5:45 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. ET, to bring both stages of Starship back intact — the first attempt at full recovery of an orbital launch system, which the company has called the “holy grail” of rocketry. The piece notes that a Super Heavy V3 booster has not yet been caught, that catching the roughly 52-metre Ship from orbit in the tower arms has never been demonstrated, and that FAA rules require showing the chance of a casualty is below 1 in 1 million. CNN.com English did not return a usable page here; this is from CNN’s Spanish edition of the same Wattles article.

items.title: Building the future — Starbase and Cochise County supercompute investments
items.summary: SpaceX’s 12 November 2026 Updates post says it is advancing two supercompute projects — a facility at Starbase in the Rio Grande Valley and a campus in Cochise County, Arizona — that together represent more than $74 billion in planned U.S. investment. It plans more than $24 billion of new supercomputing at Starbase (on top of more than $15 billion already invested there), with the site generating its own power, plus $220 million to expand Brownsville’s water and wastewater capacity by 20 million gallons a day, and a roughly $50 billion Arizona campus expected to support about 5,500 construction jobs and 1,000 permanent jobs, using dry cooling with no planned industrial groundwater use.
items.timeSource: Official SpaceX posts linking the 12 November Updates item

items.title: Not Starlink. Not Starship. This Is the Real Reason SpaceX Stock Could Soar Before 2027 Arrives. - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: Not Starlink. Not Starship. This Is the Real Reason SpaceX Stock Could Soar Before 2027 Arrives. Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A Motley Fool column by Keithen Drury, dated 12 Nov 2026 and listed in this feed as Yahoo Finance, argues that Super Intelligence — not Starlink or Starship — is the real reason SPCX could rally before 2027, noting SI revenue grew 830% year over year to $7.56 billion in Q3, more than half of SpaceX’s $14.6 billion total. He cites Musk’s view that annual recurring revenue could reach $500 billion to $1 trillion by the end of 2027, while warning that the stock could struggle if the market stays bearish on heavy AI spending.

items.title: Ukraine warns of fresh Starshield disruptions as U.S. envoys arrive in Moscow for talks with Putin - CNBC
items.snippet: Ukraine warns of fresh Starshield disruptions as U.S. envoys arrive in Moscow for talks with Putin CNBC
items.summary: A CNBC report dated 12 November 2026 says President Volodymyr Zelenskyy alleged fresh, systematic speed restrictions on SpaceX’s Starshield service over Ukraine, with terminals disconnecting above 161 km/h (100 mph) and making it harder to intercept Russian jet-powered drones along the front line and in occupied territories. CNBC says it reached out to SpaceX and the White House for comment, notes similar limits were imposed in mid-October and lifted by 24 October, and places Zelenskyy’s remarks as U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow for talks with Vladimir Putin.

items.title: Prediction: $1,000 Invested in SpaceX Today Will Be Worth This Much by 2029 - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: Prediction: $1,000 Invested in SpaceX Today Will Be Worth This Much by 2029 Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A Motley Fool column by Rick Orford, dated 12 November 2026 and carried by Yahoo Finance, sketches three earnings-based scenarios for what $1,000 in SPCX could be worth by 2029, citing Q3 revenue of $14.6 billion, $4.4 billion of net income, 13.6 million Starlink subscribers and about $19.6 billion of capex. Its conservative case (30% annual sales growth, a 20 times price-to-sales multiple) implies about $810; the base case (45%, 25 times) about $1,400; and the optimistic case (60%, 30 times) about $2,260 — the author’s calculations, not a company forecast.

items.title: USSF-627 mission

It says this was the seventh flight for the first-stage booster, which had previously launched NROL-179, SDA-T1TL-E, SDA-T1TL-A and three Starlink missions, and that after stage separation the booster landed on the Of Course I Still Love You droneship in the Pacific Ocean.

items.title: Starlink’s U.S. Speeds Rise Amid SpaceX IPO - Ookla
items.snippet: Starlink’s U.S. Speeds Rise Amid SpaceX IPO Ookla
items.summary: An Ookla analysis by Sue Marek, dated 11 Nov 2026, says Starlink’s U.S. median upload speed rose 42% year over year in the first half of 2026, from 14.63 Mbps to 20.73 Mbps, improving in all 50 states and D.C., while median download speed rose a more uneven 12% nationally to 119.71 Mbps and fell in 16 states and D.C. Ookla also found that about nine in 10 new U.S. Starlink users switched from non-fiber connections such as DSL, cable or fixed wireless, and that urban Speedtest users grew 73% year over year, more than twice the 33% rural growth.

items.title: Google's SpaceX investment takes an unexpected turn - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: Google's SpaceX investment takes an unexpected turn Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A TheStreet column by Hillary Remy and Dana Sullivan Kilroy, dated 10 Nov 2026 and listed in this feed as Yahoo Finance, says Alphabet raised its SpaceX holding to about 555 million shares, up from 551.2 million, while paying SpaceX $920 million a month for xAI data-center capacity from October 2026 through June 2029 — a contract TheStreet puts at roughly $30 billion, covering about 110,000 Nvidia GPUs. The piece notes Alphabet booked an $8.7 billion third-quarter equity-securities loss driven mainly by the SpaceX share drop, that Google called the GPU arrangement bridge capacity for Gemini (either side can exit with 90 days’ notice after 2026), and that Google executive Don Harrison has resigned from SpaceX’s board.

The mission description quoted in the article also calls for deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites and a more than 22-hour flight of about 14 orbits at roughly 275 km, longer than Flight 14’s Pacific splashdown.

items.title: 8-K — Item 5.02, departure of a director or officer
items.summary: The 8-K reports that Donald Harrison, a Class B director, resigned from the SpaceX board effective 4 Nov 2026, and that the resignation was not because of any disagreement on operations, policies, or practices. An IR note the same day thanks Harrison, who had served since February 2015 and is President of Global Partnerships and Corporate Development at Google.

items.title: Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX lose over $420 billion in combined market cap after midterms - CNBC
items.snippet: Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX lose over $420 billion in combined market cap after midterms CNBC
items.summary: CNBC reports that Tesla and SpaceX shares fell about 11% and 9% on Thursday after the midterms, taking combined market-cap losses since Tuesday’s close to more than $420 billion on concerns that Musk could face new probes and tighter regulation. The article says Musk was a major GOP donor (more than $470 million, per the Financial Times) even as most of the candidates he backed lost, and that his estimated wealth dropped to below $800 billion.

items.title: How to Invest In SpaceX (SPCX) — And How Not To - NerdWallet
items.snippet: How to Invest In SpaceX (SPCX) — And How Not To NerdWallet
items.summary: NerdWallet explains how a retail investor can buy SPCX now that SpaceX is public — and how someone who does not want the stock might still end up with exposure through funds — after the 12 Jun IPO at $135 that raised about $75 billion at a $1.75 trillion opening valuation. The guide recalls a first-day close a little above $160 and a brief spike above $225, followed by a bumpier trade often below the offer price; it is an explainer, not a recommendation.

items.title: SpaceX inks Qualcomm deal, putting Starlink closer to becoming the fourth major US wireless carrier - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: SpaceX inks Qualcomm deal, putting Starlink closer to becoming the fourth major US wireless carrier Yahoo Finance
items.summary: Yahoo Finance describes the Qualcomm agreement as a step toward making Starlink a fourth major U.S. wireless carrier, pairing satellite coverage with a terrestrial 5G build. It frames the deal as part of SpaceX’s push to add spectrum and partners after its consumer mobile offering had been limited compared with the big phone carriers.

items.title: SpaceX signs deal with Qualcomm to provide network technology for U.S. mobile service - CNBC
items.snippet: SpaceX signs deal with Qualcomm to provide network technology for U.S. mobile service CNBC
items.summary: CNBC says SpaceX struck a multiyear deal with Qualcomm to build base stations for Starlink Mobile, a planned U.S. cellular service meant to complement the satellite network, with a rollout targeted to begin next year. Financial terms were not disclosed; Qualcomm’s Durga Malladi called it a chance to advance 5G and eventually AI-native 6G, and CNBC notes Starlink already accounted for 36% of SpaceX revenue and 85% of operating profit in Q3.

items.title: Qualcomm signs major 5G infrastructure deal with SpaceX for Starlink Mobile network - Reuters
items.snippet: Qualcomm signs major 5G infrastructure deal with SpaceX for Starlink Mobile network Reuters
items.summary: Reuters reported that Qualcomm signed a major 5G-infrastructure deal with SpaceX for the Starlink Mobile network; Reuters.com itself returned 401 here. Open coverage of the same announcement, including Qualcomm’s own release and CNBC, says Qualcomm will supply radio and baseband gear for a nationwide terrestrial 5G network that complements Starlink satellites, with deployment expected to start in 2027 and financial terms undisclosed.

items.title: SpaceX Just Delivered a Monster Quarter, but the Stock Is Still Down 38% From Its High. The Reasons Are Obvious. - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: SpaceX Just Delivered a Monster Quarter, but the Stock Is Still Down 38% From Its High. The Reasons Are Obvious. Yahoo Finance
items.summary: Yahoo Finance notes that SpaceX delivered a very strong quarter but that the stock was still about 38% below its post-IPO high near $226, and it discusses why the shares had lagged the results. The column is market commentary on valuation and sentiment after the Q3 print, not a new official forecast.

items.title: 8-K — Item 8.01, Apollo GPU finance-lease commitment
items.summary: The 8-K says that on 24 Oct 2026 SpaceX signed a binding commitment for a master finance lease with an Apollo-managed lessor that will buy GPU pods and related equipment and lease them to SpaceX. The company expects about $40 billion of principal payments over roughly five-year tranche schedules, with closing targeted by year-end 2026 and deliveries in the first half of 2027; an IR release adds that the chips are next-generation NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPUs and that Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and KKR also committed.

items.title: S-8 — Cursor reoffer prospectus / S-8
items.summary: SpaceX filed a Form S-8 with a reoffer prospectus so shares issued in the Cursor acquisition can be resold by employees and other service providers, subject to Rule 144 and any lock-ups. The live EDGAR document could not be fetched here (403); contemporaneous descriptions of this filing put the registered reoffer amount at about 23.6 million Class A shares.

items.title: SpaceX reports third quarter 2026 results
items.summary: SpaceX’s official third-quarter 2026 release reports revenue of $14.6 billion, up 161% from $5.6 billion a year earlier, with net income of $4.4 billion and Adjusted EBITDA of $8.8 billion. Super Intelligence revenue was $7.56 billion and Connectivity $5.25 billion, with 13.6 million Starlink consumer subscribers and $69 monthly ARPU; the company also completed its first revenue Starship mission, deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites.

items.title: Acquisition of Cursor (Anysphere) — 8-K
items.summary: An 8-K says SpaceX closed its acquisition of Anysphere (Cursor) on 14 Aug 2026, converting outstanding Cursor stock into 389,289,254 SpaceX Class A shares at an implied $60 billion equity value, plus 1,752,426 shares for vested RSUs before tax withholding. Unvested Cursor awards were assumed as about 29.1 million SpaceX RSUs and 44.4 million options, and the merger shares were issued in an unregistered Section 4(a)(2) transaction.
items.timeSource: EDGAR acceptance of the Cursor acquisition 8-K

items.title: 8-K — Cursor (Anysphere) acquisition
items.summary: This 8-K (Items 2.01 and 3.02) reports that SpaceX completed the Anysphere/Cursor merger on 14 Aug 2026 and issued unregistered Class A shares as merger consideration. Cursor stock converted into 389,289,254 SpaceX shares at an implied $60 billion equity value, with additional shares and assumed awards for Cursor RSUs and options.

items.title: SpaceX reports second quarter 2026 results
items.summary: SpaceX’s official second-quarter 2026 release reports revenue of $7.8 billion, up 92% from $4.1 billion, a net loss of $541 million, and Adjusted EBITDA of $3.5 billion. The letter highlights two Starship V3 flight tests in 90 days, $14.1 billion of contracted cloud-services sales, the announced $60 billion Cursor deal, 12.0 million Starlink consumer subscribers at $66 ARPU, $47.5 billion of backlog, and $100 billion of cash and marketable securities after the IPO.

items.title: SpaceX closes IPO, including full exercise of underwriters’ option
items.summary: SpaceX’s IR release says the IPO closed on 15 Jun 2026 with 638,888,888 Class A shares issued, including the full underwriters’ option for 83,333,333 extra shares, for about $85.7 billion of gross proceeds. Class A shares had begun trading on 12 Jun 2026 on the Nasdaq Global Select Market and Nasdaq Texas under the ticker SPCX.
items.timeSource: datePublished on the official IR release page

items.title: SpaceX prices IPO at $135.00 per share
items.summary: SpaceX priced 555,555,555 Class A shares at $135.00 and granted the underwriters a 30-day option to buy up to 83,333,333 more shares at the same price. The IR release said trading was expected to start on 12 Jun 2026 on Nasdaq Global Select and Nasdaq Texas under SPCX, with closing slated for 15 Jun 2026.
items.timeSource: datePublished on the official IR release page

items.title: SpaceX launches initial public offering roadshow
items.summary: SpaceX launched the IPO roadshow for 555,555,555 Class A shares, with an expected $135.00 offer price and the intended ticker SPCX on Nasdaq Global Select and Nasdaq Texas. The company also planned to grant underwriters a 30-day option for up to 83,333,333 additional shares.
